prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: none is always best — pick the platform that fits your trip type and priorities, and use the same process on any site to vet hosts. Below is a compact guide to when to choose each platform, plus practical steps and checklists for finding a reliable host and avoiding scams.

Which platform to choose (by trip type)
- Want a unique local stay, experiences host interaction, shared spaces, or long-stay monthly discounts: Airbnb.
- Need a whole-home rental for families/groups and listings focused on full properties: Vrbo (good for vacation-home owners).
- Want hotels + apartments on one site, lots of instant-book options, and flexible cancellation policies: Booking.com.
- Last-minute hotel-like bookings or multi-type comparisons (hotel vs apartment): Booking.com tends to be easiest.
- If you need guaranteed whole-home only for a family/group: prefer Vrbo or filter “entire place” on Airbnb.

Platform tradeoffs (quick)
- Airbnb: large selection, unique stays, strong host/guest community features, service fees, Guest Refund/Support; look for “Superhost” and verified listings.
- Vrbo: mostly whole-home rentals, good for families and large groups; sometimes fewer small/unique listings; owner-operated listings.
- Booking.com: wide hotel + rental inventory, instant booking common, sometimes simpler cancellation rules; price display can be confusing (watch total cost).

How to find a good host (step-by-step)
1. Filter and shortlist
   - Set must-have filters: entire place (if needed), number of beds, wifi, pet policy, parking, self check-in, etc.
   - Sort by review score or “recommended” and also check map for neighborhood convenience.

2. Read reviews strategically
   - Prioritize recent reviews (last 6–12 months).
   - Look for repeated themes: cleanliness, accuracy of listing photos, host responsiveness, quiet/noise, check-in smoothness.
   - A single small complaint is OK; multiple similar complaints = red flag.

3. Check host profile and badges
   - Look for Superhost / Premier Host / Experienced Host / Verified ID and lots of completed stays.
   - Read host replies in reviews — shows how they handle problems.

4. Inspect listing details carefully
   - Compare photos to the description; check availability calendar history (gaps may show frequent cancellations).
   - Note cleaning fee, security deposit, and total price (not just nightly rate).
   - Confirm exact location policy (many platforms hide the exact address until booking).

5. Ask focused questions before booking
   - Example questions: “Is check-in self-service or will someone meet us?”, “Is the Wi‑Fi speed reliable?”, “Where exactly is the parking? Any height restrictions?”, “Are there building rules about noise/guests?”, “Has anything changed since the photos were taken?”
   - If you get slow/defensive/unclear replies, consider other options.

6. Watch for red flags/scams
   - Host asks to communicate or pay off-platform (wire transfer, Venmo, cash) — never do this.
   - Price way below market with poor/no reviews, inconsistent photos, or empty host profile.
   - Last-minute requests to share personal info beyond what platform requires.

What a good host looks/acts like
- Quick, polite responses (within 24 hours or sooner for near dates).
- Clear house rules, accurate photos and description, straightforward fees.
- Provides a house manual or local guide and clear check-in instructions (keypad, lockbox, meet-and-greet).
- Proactively addresses issues and responds reasonably to problems.
- Strong recent reviews praising cleanliness, communication, and accuracy.

Booking and safety checklist before paying
- Confirm total price (nightly + cleaning + service fees + taxes + refundable deposit).
- Read cancellation policy and consider travel insurance or refundable rates for uncertain plans.
- Pay only through the platform and use a credit card.
- Save/copy the listing, host messages, and payment receipts.
- Check city short-term rental rules if that matters to you (some cities have restrictions).

Negotiation and messaging tips
- For longer stays or off-peak dates, politely ask: “Would you consider a discount for a 7+ night stay?” Offer quick facts that build trust: “We’re two professionals, non-smokers, respectful — booked X times on [platform] with 5-star reviews.”
- Be concise and specific. Example message template:
  “Hi [Host name], we’re [number] guests traveling for [reason]. Dates: [dates]. Quick questions: Is check-in self-check-in or will someone meet us? Is parking available? Is the Wi‑Fi reliable for work? Thank you — we look forward to hearing from you.”

If you’re unsure, do a side-by-side comparison
- Open the same dates and filters on 2–3 platforms and compare total price, cancellation, and host responsiveness. Booking.com for instant confirmation vs Airbnb/Vrbo for host-managed options.

If you want, tell me:
- trip dates, party size, location, and what’s most important (price, family-friendly, pet-friendly, workspace, neighborhood) — I can suggest which platform and help draft a message to a host or shortlist specific items to look for.
